correctness.rationale: A set of ground edges dominates its line graph exactly when at most one ground label is unused: an edge on two missing labels is undominated and every other edge meets a selected one. The three distinct edges underlying a path object are connected, so cover at most four labels. To attain the resulting ceiling use disjoint four-label trees, with one final triangle on the last one, two or three required labels padded by old labels as needed, or a tree on the last four. The small orders 3, 4 and 5 admit one such object. At tight orders equality forces pairwise disjoint four-label supports and one hole. Each support gives 4·3 star choices with designated middle and 4!/2 ordinary paths, so the 24 cancels the 4! in the block partition count. With one path removed its replacement must occupy four of the five free labels; the 120 choices include the original exactly once, and neighbors obtained by dropping different paths cannot coincide. Hole swaps permit all ground-label permutations of block memberships and within-block moves select the decorations. Hence the connected graph has degree 119k and the stated edge count. The phrase 'last three-edge tree' in the construction is superseded immediately by the explicit triangle construction for one through three residual labels; that construction is valid under the non-induced convention.
residual_risks: The recorded direct small-order check only samples exchange degrees for n=9. The all-order proof, not the sampled degrees or product enumeration, establishes regularity and connectivity.
